rule_audit.name: Prohibited self-help recovery of possession or rent
rule_audit.label: Prohibited self-help recovery of possession or rent (R.C. 5321.15)
rule_audit.summary: A residential landlord may not recover possession through utility termination, exclusion, or other unlawful acts, and may not seize tenant property for rent without a court order.
rule_audit.excerpt: the residence several times, all to oust Alice. And on February 28, 2005, Edwin Cazeau issued Alice a statutory notice to quit the premises in three days but the door locks had already been changed. RC § 5321.15 provides that a person entitled to immediate possession of a residential dwelling can not exclude a tenant from the premises and can obtain possession only as provided in RC Chapter 1923. A person that violates RC § 5321.15 is liable for all damages caused as well as reasonable attorney

elements.label: Residential landlord-tenant relationship
elements.requirement: Identify residential premises landlord and tenant or former tenant in possession.
elements.explanation: The brief identifies a residential premises (815 Red Hill Drive), Edwin as the person entitled to possession, and Alice as an occupant whom the brief characterizes as a tenant at sufferance. elements.quote: Alice Stone's status in Cazeau's Red Hill residence was that of an occupant staying at the will or sufferance of Cazeau. While Cazeau could revoke or terminate Alice's at will occupation of his property, he was statutorily prohibited from distraining her property and access to the residence without process. Alice Stone's status could change once Cazeau had expressed his "will" to end and no longer "suffer" her occupation. That is, her status would then become one of a tenant at sufferance.

By her own writing, Defendant Cathryn Nixon has admitted that she excluded Alice Stone. See exhibits one and two of Alice Stone Affidavit, saying to Alice "[D]o not enter the house [.]" and that "[All] lock (sic) have been changed." And this wrongful exclusion occurred not once but on three distinct occasions.

rule_audit.name: Notice to leave the premises
rule_audit.label: Notice to leave the premises (R.C. 1923.04)
rule_audit.summary: A forcible entry and detainer action requires that the party seeking possession first serve a notice to leave the premises, in the statutory form and by a permitted method, and then wait the statutory period before filing.
rule_audit.source: R.C. 1923.04; Iskin, Ohio Eviction and Landlord-Tenant Law (6th ed. 2022), § I.C
rule_audit.excerpt: and June, 2006. On June 14, 2006 STJ, through its agent Appellee Dayton Rental, delivered to Ealy and his wife a statutory three-day Notice to Leave the Premises in accordance with Ohio Revised Code Section 1923.04. (See Exhibit "A" to STJ's Complaint) by leaving such Notice at the premises. Ealy appeared before the Magistrate at the first hearing on July 21, 2006 and admitted that Ealy and his wife did not pay rent for May or June, 2006 in accordance with the terms of the lease. This creates a concrete support concern without establishing a filing-level defect.

tests.reason: The supplied passage shows that the holdover exception under R.C. 5321.03(A)(4) was at issue, while the challenge states that the brief acknowledges no R.C. 5321.02 counterclaim and focuses its response on fair-housing claims. That creates a concrete concern that the exception analysis does not address the relevant statutory claim, but the supplied excerpt is insufficient to establish a mandatory correction.

rule_audit.name: Notice to leave the premises
rule_audit.label: Notice to leave the premises (R.C. 1923.04)
rule_audit.summary: A forcible entry and detainer action requires that the party seeking possession first serve a notice to leave the premises, in the statutory form and by a permitted method, and then wait the statutory period before filing.
rule_audit.source: R.C. 1923.04; Iskin, Ohio Eviction and Landlord-Tenant Law (6th ed. 2022), § I.C
rule_audit.excerpt: sten with an eighty-one day notice of nonrenewal of lease, effective September 30, 2011. When Masten did not timely vacate the premises, K&D served her with a three day notice to vacate pursuant to O.R.C. § 1923.04 for the reason that Defendant was a holdover tenant. On October 14, 2011 K& D filed a Complaint for forcible entry and detainer in Euclid Municipal Court. A tenant raising it has to identify the protected act, the retaliatory act, and the connection between them.

tests.claim: Identify residential premises landlord and tenant or former tenant in possession.
tests.problem: The brief does not plead a residential landlord-tenant relationship; it affirmatively argues that Lee was an employee-accommodated occupant rather than a tenant because there was no rental agreement or rent payment. The cited authorities support the brief's legal position that those asserted facts do not establish tenancy, rather than supporting this element.
tests.reason: Opponent did not establish a filing defect. The supplied passage shows the brief affirmatively disputes the landlord-tenant element as part of its legal position; a brief arguing that no tenancy existed need not plead the contrary relationship.

tests.claim: Identify exclusion utility or service termination unlawful threat or seizure without required judicial process.
tests.problem: The brief identifies the alleged recovery of possession by stating that Lee was terminated and asked to leave immediately, and it discusses exclusion and lockout as prohibited methods under the statute. It does not establish that appellees used an exclusion, utility termination, unlawful threat, seizure, or another prohibited self-help act; instead, it asserts their removal of Lee was lawful.
tests.reason: Opponent did not establish that the brief was required to concede or establish a prohibited self-help act. The supplied passage identifies the asserted departure circumstances, while the stated brief position is that appellees' conduct was lawful.

tests.claim: Plead actual harm causally resulting from the prohibited act.
tests.problem: The brief does not plead that Lee suffered actual damages caused by a prohibited recovery act. It addresses only whether Lee could maintain a wrongful-eviction claim and argues that appellees did nothing wrongful.
tests.reason: Opponent did not establish a defect because the brief argues against liability for wrongful eviction rather than advancing a claim requiring Lee to plead and prove damages from a prohibited act.

Opponent has not established a defect.
